cross_cutting_mbo_finding.headline: A THIN SESSION COMPRESSES NET AND DOES NOT COMPRESS RANGE. My own round-1 sanity check assumed both scale together (sqrt of participation) and that is the one assumption on my day that the tape falsified. The NET half was right - I called +60 against +30 on a derived holiday sigma of ~360. The RANGE half was wrong by roughly a factor of two, and it is wrong for the same reason my displacement-efficiency instrument exists: when participation falls, price per unit of flow rises roughly as fast, so the excursions survive even though the net does not.

1_the_range_vs_net_asymmetry_the_r2_corr.what_r1_asserted: 'A holiday session running roughly 30% of a normal session's trade count scales sigma by sqrt(0.30) = 0.55, so the holiday-session sigma is about 360.' I then applied that same scaling implicitly to the PATH and carried a p50 peak of +250 from the anchor, declining the excursion beyond it as 'a reactive tail on a partial session, not mine to bank'.
1_the_range_vs_net_asymmetry_the_r2_corr.what_the_tape_says: The NET scaling held: realized day-move +30 against a derived sigma of 360 is 0.08 sigma - a nothing day, exactly as called. The RANGE scaling did not: the session's realized range is 1,140 (high 3.096 at 09:30, low 2.982 at 23:30) against n0_range_20_mean 1,094. A partial session with roughly 30% participation printed a FULL-SIZE regime range. Compression 1.04x, not 0.55x.
1_the_range_vs_net_asymmetry_the_r2_corr.why_this_is_a_mechanism_and_not_an_excus: It is my own instrument turned on the whole session instead of only on the gap. Reopen displacement efficiency says a thin book moves multiples of the price per unit of flow. If price-per-flow scales as roughly 1/participation while flow scales as participation, then RANGE (a price quantity driven by the largest single directional tranche) is first-order invariant to participation, while NET (a price quantity driven by the residual after two-sided cancellation) falls with participation because there are fewer independent tranches to cancel against. One mechanism predicts both halves, and it predicts exactly the asymmetry observed: net 0.08 sigma, range 1.04x.
1_the_range_vs_net_asymmetry_the_r2_corr.the_consequence_I_got_wrong_in_r1: Because I scaled the path with the net, my p50 peak sat at +250 against a realized +620 excursion and I justified the shortfall by calling the excursion 'reactive'. That classification is wrong on its own evidence. The 0525 push is a MECHANICAL, DEADLINE-BOUND buyer (NGN26 roll-in ahead of the 05-27 NGM26 expiry) that MUST execute before a 13:00 early close, in a book at ~30% participation. A deadline-constrained buyer in a thin book is a MECHANISM for an overshoot-and-full-give-back, not a reaction to news. Everything needed to say so was in the r1 read; I named the deadline, named the thin book, named the single liquid window, and then declined the consequence.
1_the_range_vs_net_asymmetry_the_r2_corr.the_general_form_proposed: THIN_SESSION_RANGE_INVARIANCE (+n): on holiday / partial / early-close sessions, size the DAY-NET by participation-scaled sigma (sqrt rule, confirmed here) but size the PATH RANGE at the UNSCALED regime range (n0_range_20_mean). Corollary: on such a session the p50 path must carry a full-size excursion with a full-size give-back, because the flow that makes the excursion is one deadline-bound tranche that has no counterparty to hold it.
1_the_range_vs_net_asymmetry_the_r2_corr.n_and_limits: n=1 for the range half within this block (0525 is G20's only partial session), plus n=2 for the underlying displacement-efficiency mechanism (0524 stub 15.4x, 0531 stub 24.6x). PROPOSAL. Needs a second holiday/early-close session in another block. Falsifiable directly: any thin session whose realized range compresses with sqrt(participation) kills it.

2_answering_B_s_question_can_a_SEAM_BRID.the_question_as_B_put_it: B's cross-cutting finding measures that the blind's CONSTRUCTED chain read cum -830 / polarity DOWN at the 0531 seam against a realized +2,390 / polarity UP - inverted at the exact seam where extension mattered - and asks whether a bridge can detect that without price. B's proposed chain_staleness_gate explicitly says it has no price-free TRIGGER, only a bound. I tested three candidate channels on the actual seam and two of them FAIL. Naming the failures matters more than the one that works, because one of the failures is my own instrument.
2_answering_B_s_question_can_a_SEAM_BRID.channel_1_COT_FAILS_and_it_is_MY_instrum: The cot channel does NOT detect it, and I have to say so because the joint cot_residual_consumption_window is mine. The live publication at the 0531 seam is report date 2026-05-19 -> superseded by report 2026-05-26 published 2026-05-29T15:30. Its report WINDOW is 05-20 through 05-26 - it PREDATES the 0527/0528 covering ramp entirely. Over its own window the constructed chain and the position data are perfectly COHERENT: price fell (0522 realized -1,000, 0525 +30, 0526 -190) and managed money ADDED 38,123 of short. Falling price plus shorts adding is aligned delivery. There is no incoherence to detect. The COT is simply too slow: at a seam it tells you a residual EXISTS, it cannot tell you the chain that ran while the residual sat there is inverted. Any construction that claims otherwise is back-dating the ramp into a report that does not contain it.
2_answering_B_s_question_can_a_SEAM_BRID.channel_2_per_day_flow_conviction_on_the: flow_conviction = sign(never-masked session sflow) x sign(the blind's OWN constructed day-move) is fully price-free and computable at the seam. Run across the four sessions into the seam: 0526 sflow -1,290 vs constructed -280 = ALIGNED; 0527 -4,910 vs -500 = ALIGNED; 0528 -1,966 vs +150 = NEGATIVE; 0529 -2,126 vs -380 = ALIGNED. The reading IMMEDIATELY before the seam is aligned-down and AGREES with the constructed chain. A most-recent-reading test does not fire. It only fires if you privilege 0528 (the catalyst session, and the block's largest phase volume at 88,726) over 0529, which is a weighting choice made with hindsight. FAILS as stated.

channel_3_the_CUMULATIVE_IMPACT_INTEGRAL.construction: Over the window since the last realized anchor, compute IMPACT = |sum of the blind's own constructed day-moves| / |sum of the never-masked session signed flow|. Both terms are available to a price-masked blind: the numerator is its own forecast, the denominator is the MBO firehose. Compare against the block's own reference impact taken on a session with NO absorption anywhere.
channel_3_the_CUMULATIVE_IMPACT_INTEGRAL.the_numbers_at_the_0531_seam: Window 0526-0529: constructed cum change -280 -500 +150 -380 = -1,010, against a signed-flow integral of -1,290 -4,910 -1,966 -2,126 = -9,198. IMPACT = 0.110. Reference: 0525 is the block's ONLY session with ph_absorb FALSE on all three phases AND absorb_session FALSE - the one clean un-absorbed session - and the blind's own constructed +180 on sflow +1,094 gives IMPACT 0.165.
channel_3_the_CUMULATIVE_IMPACT_INTEGRAL.the_read: The blind's own arithmetic asserts that four consecutive sessions of one-sided sell aggression, with flow magnitude rising to 8x the reference session, bought only 67% of the reference price impact per unit. Sustained one-sided aggression delivering PROGRESSIVELY LESS price per unit is the definition of an absorbing passive side, and direction.absorption_is_reversal (0.85) is unambiguous about what an absorbed sell means. The blind asserted a DOWN chain while its own numbers described a bid absorbing 9,198 units of sell.
channel_3_the_CUMULATIVE_IMPACT_INTEGRAL.honest_weakness: 0.110 against 0.165 is a 33% deficit, not a chasm, and the reference is n=1 within the block. The per-day ratios are noisy (0525 0.165, 0526 0.217, 0527 0.102, 0528 0.076, 0529 0.179) - the signal is the four-session INTEGRAL, not any single day. I am NOT claiming a threshold. PROPOSAL: compute the same integral and the same un-absorbed reference on G19 and G21 to establish whether an un-absorbed regime band exists at all. If it does, this is the price-free trigger B's chain_staleness_gate says it lacks; if it does not, the gate keeps its bound and this dies.

2_answering_B_s_question_can_a_SEAM_BRID.the_bridge_s_actual_strongest_price_free: It is the REOPEN STUB. At the 0531 seam the stub printed session_signed_flow +278 with session_b_share 0.513 - the FIRST net-BUY session after four consecutive net-sell sessions (0526 -1,290, 0527 -4,910, 0528 -1,966, 0529 -2,126). A change in the sign of the AGGRESSOR side is directly observable in never-masked tape_conditions, needs no price at all, and is the operationally decisive half. HONEST SCOPE: it does NOT detect what B measured. B measured a LEVEL error (cum -830 vs +2,390); the stub detects a forward POLARITY change. A bridge cannot recover a level it was never given. It can tell the receiving owner that the side which has been aggressing for four sessions has just stopped - which on 0601 was true and was worth the whole day.
2_answering_B_s_question_can_a_SEAM_BRID.what_this_means_for_B_s_gate: I support chain_staleness_gate and I am NOT proposing a rival. I am supplying one candidate trigger (channel 3, weak, forward-testable) and I am RULING OUT two channels including my own COT instrument, so the merge does not adopt a gate believing it has three price-free triggers when it has at most one.

The seller was substantially DONE inside the stub itself. So the low belongs in the FIRST QUARTER of ph1, ~23:00-00:00, not at its end. Round-2 correction, derived from the incoming state, not from the realized low.

MY_CORRECTION_BACK_the_hinge_tell_needs_.B_s_tell_as_stated: 'At a covering-to-distribution turn, the crossover phase prints NET FLOW NEAR ZERO ON UNUSUALLY HIGH VOLUME, and it is the LAST phase before the flip.'
MY_CORRECTION_BACK_the_hinge_tell_needs_.the_gap_in_it: As stated, (volume high, net ~0) is ambiguous. That cell also contains ordinary BALANCE - a high-volume phase where two-sided aggression cancels and the price goes NOWHERE. A balance phase is a consolidation, not a handover, and it predicts nothing. What makes 0529 ph3 a handover is the THIRD term: it moved -810, a full session's worth of price, on essentially zero net aggression. Price displacement without net aggression is the passive side moving, and a passive side that moves that far in one phase is a passive side changing hands.
MY_CORRECTION_BACK_the_hinge_tell_needs_.the_corrected_form: Read the TRIPLE (volume, net, price), not the pair. HIGH VOLUME + NET ~ 0 + LARGE PRICE MOVE = aggression handover (the passive side changed sides). HIGH VOLUME + NET ~ 0 + SMALL PRICE MOVE = balance/consolidation, no information. This is the same move I made against E - read the pair, not the scalar - carried one term further, and it is the natural extension of the four-way (volume, net) form B adopted from me.
MY_CORRECTION_BACK_the_hinge_tell_needs_.B_s_own_honest_limit_supports_it: B flags that the block's later reversal (0602 -> 0603, aggression flipping back to net sell as price rose) shows NO clean hinge phase, and declines to claim it fires at every turn. The price term is a candidate explanation for that: without it, the tell has no way to distinguish a turn that had a handover phase from one that did not. Adding the price condition makes the non-fires PREDICTED rather than merely admitted, which is what a general tell has to do.
